sources.said: This initiative will provide support to Ugandan production companies and individuals for the development of Audio-visual content. This includes feature films, short films, animations, documentaries, and television dramas. ... This financial year 2020/2021, the Commission has prioritized support for development and production of local films/audio-visual content which promotes Ugandan culture and tourism. ... The Programme does not support the following: Corporate videos; Non-governmental organisations and other institutions or companies not primarily involved in the film and television industry; Individuals or companies who are not Ugandan citizens; Training programmes primarily focusing on the performing arts ... Successful applicants or beneficiaries have a one-year period (financial year) to raise and utilise the approved support. Failure to do so will result in the automatic forfeiture of such support

UG.notes: Uganda: stage plays are licensed under Cap 49 (1943) with permits from the Broadcasting Council; the copyright law sets no rate; UNCC (the National Theatre) is unreachable (502) and the Daily Monitor and ULII sit behind Cloudflare.
